diagnostic_to_validation.descriptive_conclusion: Scalar's safe-crawling/incomplete regime reproduced exactly at the pooled level (0 feasible and 0 completed in both splits; 53 incomplete-safe plus 1 incomplete speed-violation episode). Constrained retained timely feasible completion, although Validation had 23 feasible episodes versus 28 on Diagnostic and more speed violations (8 versus 1).

interrupted_finalizer_recovery.description: The initial matrix invocation completed C11/C29/C47, then stopped before any Scalar episode because FSRL's extra-state loader rejected the Scalar checkpoint's empty None state. The completed Constrained artifacts were preserved. A continuation evaluated only untouched S11/S29/S47 after representing the unused empty Lagrangian state as an empty mapping; actor parameters matched the frozen Diagnostic hashes. No condition was repeated.

scalar_failure_regime.constraint_avoidance: Scalar was speed-compliant in 53/54 episodes but completed 0/54; this is constraint avoidance, not successful completion under constraints.

scientific_interpretation.causal_limit: The result does not establish that constrained optimization alone causes the full difference: adaptive multipliers, separate reward/cost critics, FSRL critic entropy semantics, and actor-loss structure also differ.
scientific_interpretation.deadline_signal_conclusion: The earlier Constrained-V2 improvement cannot be attributed solely to access to the deadline-feasibility signal.
scientific_interpretation.supported: In this benchmark, supplying the same energy, speed-constraint, and dense deadline-feasibility information through a strong fixed scalar reward is insufficient to match explicit constrained learning.

strong_control_fairness.selection_statement: The lambda weights were not chosen from the present Diagnostic or Validation performance; the Scalar control was deliberately strong.
strong_control_fairness.statement: Scalar SAC received a reference-informed fixed scalarization derived from previously completed Constrained runs.
